name: Concrete Nouns 200
description: A set of concrete nouns spanning common semantic fields and relations.

concepts.definition: A reptile belonging to the subfamily Alligatorinae in the family Alligatoridae in the order Crocodylia.

Any insectivorous anuran amphibian of the family Ranidae, such as Rana temporaria of Europe, having a short squat tailless body with a moist smooth skin and very long hind legs specialized for hopping.

Any reptile of the suborder Lacertilia, especially those of the family Lacertidae, typically having an elongated body, four limbs, and a small tail: includes the gechos, iguanas, chameleons, monitors, and slow worms.
Any reptile of the suborder Serpentes, typically having a scaly cylindrical limbless body, fused eyelids, and a jaw modified for swallowing large prey.
A reptile of the order Testudines (the crown group of the superorder Chelonia), characterised by a special bony or cartilaginous shell developed from their ribs that acts as a shield.
An enclosed heated compartment usually lined with a refractory material used for baking or drying substances, firing ceramics, heat-treating, etc.
An electronic device used for calling people.
A device that can capture the signal sent over radio waves and render the modulated signal as sound.
A chamber within which a fuel-air mixture is burned to provide heat, the heat itself being radiated outward from the chamber; used for space heating, process-fluid heating, and steel blast furnaces.
A device for receiving television signals and displaying them in visual form.
An electrical appliance used for toasting, mostly bread.
A bird, usually black, of the genus Corvus, having a strong conical beak, with projecting bristles; it has a harsh, croaking call.
One of several birds of the family Columbidae.
Any of several large carnivorous birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.
A bird of prey of genus Falco, which kill preys with its beak (unlike Accipitridae as eagles and hawks, which kill with its feet).
Waterfowl of the Anatidae family.
A predatory bird of the family Accipitridae.
A solitary, mainly nocturnal bird of prey, belonging to the order Strigiformes; it has large forward-facing eyes and ears and a hawk-like beak, and it can turn its head 180 degrees around.
Aquatic, flightless birds.
Bird of the family Phasianidae.

The European robin (Erithacus rubecula), most commonly known in Anglophone Europe simply as the robin, is a small insectivorous passerine bird, specifically a chat, that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family (Turdidae), but is now considered to be an Old World flycatcher.
A small song bird, in the family Passeridae.
Bird of the family Anatidae.
Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae.
Part of the Picidae family, a group of near-passerine birds that also consist of piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers.
A place where people who are ill or injured are treated and taken care of by doctors and nurses.
A library is a collection of sources of information and similar resources, made accessible to a defined community for reference or borrowing.
An upper garment, which resembles a shirt, worn usually by women and girls.
A long outer garment worn over the shoulders covering the back; a cape, often with a hood.
An outer garment covering the upper torso and arms.
A one-piece garment for a woman that has a skirt and a body section.
A garment for a hand, often extending to the wrist and sometimes up to the elbow, which either covers each finger individually, or separates the thumb from the other fingers.
An item of clothing intended to cover the head made from material hard enough to have a shape independant of the skull, and most commonly with a rim.
A mid-stomach–length garment for the upper body.
A garment, usually consisting of a long piece of cloth, wound around the head or neck or shoulders.
An article of clothing that is worn on the upper part of the body, and often has sleeves, either long or short, that cover the arms.
A knitted jacket or pullover, usually warm and long-sleeved.
A piece of clothing for the upper body without sleeves and usually worn over a shirt.
A container that stores things and is small enough so that one can wear it.
A container, typically made of glass and having a tapered neck, used for holding liquids.
A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items.
A generic man-made object with space in it (commonly made of cardboard or wood) that is used to keep and store many various different objects.
A vessel used for cooking or storing food or liquids.
The popular, crisp, round fruit of the apple tree, usually with red, yellow or green skin, light-coloured flesh and pips inside.
A fruit of orange color with a fuzzy peel and a black seed inside, similar to a peach or plum of a tree from the family Prunus armeniaca.
The fruit of the banana tree.
Fruit of the Cherry tree.
The large hard-shelled oval nut with a fibrous husk of the cocos palm.
The red and typically sour berry of several evergreen shrubs in the family Ericaceae.
A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on certain vines.
Fruit with yellow rind and acidic/sour juice.
A green citrus fruit.
The soft, sweet, juicy fruit of the peach tree, usually with a red or orange skin, yellow flesh and a large stone inside.
A fruit produced by the pear tree.
A tropical plant with edible multiple fruit consisting of coalesced berries, also called pineapples, and the most economically significant plant in the Bromeliaceae family.
Soft, red fruit with yellow seeds on its surface.
A piece of furniture, made for a person to sleep on.
An item of furniture comprising a seat, legs, back, and sometimes arm rests, on which or in which one people can sit.
A piece of furniture that generally consists of a hard, flat, horizontal surface, which is elevated and stabilised by 3 or more legs (usually 4).
Piece of furniture usually stuffed and used for seating two or more persons.
A piece of furniture that generally consists of a hard, flat, horizontal surface, which is elevated and stabilised by 3 or more legs (usually 4).
Large object, often made out of wood, used for storing clothes or other fabrics.
A large beast of prey of the family Ursidae, related to the dog and raccoon, having shaggy hair, a very small tail, and flat feet.
A mammal of the genus Castor, having a wide, flat tail and webbed feet.
Male bovine animal.
A common four-legged animal (Felis silvestris) that is often kept as a household pet.
Female bovine animal (Bos taurus) of the subfamily Bovinae of the family Bovidae.
(Canis latrans) A member of the Canidae family native to North America.
The common name for 41 species of even-toed ungulates that compose the family Cervidae in the order Artiodactyla; males have antlers.
A domesticated animal, Equus asinus.
A mammal of the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and two large ivory tusks jutting from the upper jaw. Elephants are the largest land animals now existing.
A carnivorous relatively small canine of the species Vulpes Vulpes.
A quadruped animal native to Africa, remarkable for the length of its legs and neck.
A common four-legged animal (Capra) that is related to sheep and bred by humans for its coat and milk.
Large, African ape covered in dark hair.
A large animal with four legs of the Equus caballus species which people ride on or use for carrying things or pulling vehicles.
A large cat (Panthera leo) that is native to Africa, Asia and formerly much of Europe.
A common, four-legged animal (Sus scrofa) that has cloven hooves, bristles and a nose adapted for digging and is farmed by humans for its meat.
One of several small mammals of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail.
A nearly omnivorous rodent of the genus ''rattus'' characterised by a long hairless tail, rounded ears, and a pointed nose.
A common, four-legged animal (Ovis) that is commonly kept by humans for its wool.
A small or medium-sized rodent of the family Sciuridae.
A large carnivorous animal (Panthera tigris) of the cat family indigenous to Asia.
Any of the black, red, brown, or yellow insects of the family Formicidae characterized by a large head and by living in organized colonies.
A group of insects which are biologically classified in the order Coleoptera /koʊliːˈɒptərə/.
A lepidopteran that is active at day.
The most primitive of the living winged insects.
A plant-eating insect with long back legs that can jump very high and makes a sharp high noise using its back legs or wings.
A large wasp that can inflict a severe sting, characteristically building large papery nests.
Group of insects related to butterflies.
A flying stinging insect related to the bee, which is usually coloured yellow and black.
A musical instrument of the woodwind family.
Musical instrument with usually six strings.
A large musical instrument with a row of black and white keys that are pressed to play notes.
A musical instrument of the woodwind class consisting of a curved metal tube with finger keys and a mouthpiece.
A musical instrument in the brass family.
A small, wooden and bowed stringed musical instrument with four strings.
A tool for felling trees or chopping wood consisting of a heavy metallic or stone head flattened to a blade on one side, and which is attached to a usually wooden handle.
A tool with a cutting edge at the end.
A utensil with spikes used to put solid food into the mouth.
A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.

A utensil consisting of a sharpened piece of hard material such as steel or other metal, ceramic, glass or stone, usually attached to a handle, that is formed in a manner that allows for cutting softer materials, especially meat or other food.
A garden tool with a row of pointed teeth fixed to a long handle, used for collecting grass or debris, or for loosening soil.
A tool with a toothed blade used for cutting hard substances, in particular wood or metal.
A hand tool used for driving screws.

A tool consisting of a stick (usually out of wood) and a bigger, slightly humped surface (usually out of metal), which is used to move material such as earth, snow, grain, etc. from one place to another.
A device for separating wanted elements from unwanted material.
Tool having a flat and sharp metal tip and a wooden handle used to break, dig and move the earth.
An implement for eating or serving, a small bowl with a long straight handle.
A tree of the genus Betula, with small leaves and a trunk that is white with darker blotches.
A common name for various coniferous trees or shrubs of northern temperate regions that belong to the family Cupressaceae.
A tall tree with broad leaves.

Any tree of the genus Quercus in the order Fagales, characterized by simple, usually lobed leaves, scaly winter buds, a star-shaped pith, and its fruit, the acorn, which is a nut; the wood is tough, hard, and durable, generally having a distinct pattern.
Evergreen coniferous tree of the genus Pinus.
Any of various deciduous trees of the genus Populus.
Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix.
A plant of the cabbage family, Brassicaceae, which is shaped like a tree.
An edible plant, Brassica oleracea, with many varieties.
Domesticated root vegetable usually orange or red in colour.
One of several vegetables in the species Brassica oleracea in the genus Brassica.
A vegetable with a long greenish stalk of the carrot family.
A type of grain of the species Zea mays.
The edible fruit of the cucumber plant, having a green rind and crisp white flesh.
A species in the onion genus, Allium.
A often green plant, Lactuca sativa, which is mainly used in salads.
A vegetable and is the most widely cultivated species of the genus Allium.
A tuberous plant, Solanum tuberosum, often eaten as a starchy vegetable, particularly in the Americas and Europe.
An edible root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family that was domesticated in Europe in pre-Roman times.
An important leaf vegetable, grown throughout the temperate regions of the world.
A cultivated Eurasian plant, Brassica rapa, of the mustard family, whose whitish root and leaves are edible.
A vehicle that is equipped for taking sick or injured people to and from hospital, especially in case of emergencies.
A large, long-bodied motor vehicle equipped with seating for passengers, usually operating as part of a scheduled service.
A four-wheeled motor vehicle used for land transport, usually propelled by a gasoline or diesel internal combustion engine.
A transport ship used for small distances from one port to another which often runs on a regular schedule.
A type of rotorcraft in which lift and thrust are supplied by rotors.
Single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.
A self-propelled, connected group of vehicles moving on rails.
A large and heavy road vehicle designed for the transportation of goods, materials, or troops.
Oily freshwater fish from the family Cyprinidae.
Any of ray-finned fish with long stiff barbels, resembling a cat's whiskers. There are diverse types of catfish, ranging in size and appearance and inhabiting mostly freshwater environments.
A carnivorous aquatic mammal inhabiting mostly in the shallower seas of the continental shelves.
One of several species of fish of the Salmonidae family.
Fresh water salmon.
Large marine mammals of the order Cetacea; the body is streamlined, the broad flat tail is used for propulsion, and the limbs are balancing structures.
A device filled with explosives used for destroying things.
A bullet firing weapon mounted on a carriage.
A bullet firing weapon to be held in the hands or arms.
a long, stabbing weapon for thrusting or throwing, consisting of a wooden shaft to which a sharp-pointed head, as of iron or steel, is attached.
A long-bladed weapon that has a handle (and sometimes a hilt) and is designed to stab, cut or slash.
